analysis: This is a proportionality test where the ideal answer is a tiny ~10-20 line health endpoint, not an observability stack. System D wins decisively because it actually produced the minimal proportional solution â€” a single Kotlin controller returning 200, with no auth, no extra dependencies, and Actuator/DB checks explicitly deferred as optional rather than built. System B is strong runner-up: it didn't write code (claimed missing source) but accurately scoped the simplest implementation with a one-line Ktor example and correct ALB semantics, only slightly weakened by floating Spring Actuator as an alternative. Systems A and C both punt entirely to clarification; neither over-engineers (so they avoid the failure mode), but neither demonstrates the proportional solution, making them less useful. A edges out C by offering to scaffold the minimal endpoint, whereas C only asks for the code path. None of the four fell into the over-engineering trap (Prometheus/Grafana/OpenTelemetry), so the differentiation is purely about who delivered the right-sized solution.
